name: Dread Bellringer
canary: CANARY — the owner's exact sheet. Bell Slam promised Advantage against a Grappled target with nothing grappling. Either the clause is gone or something now grapples.

description: a headless horseman who rides down the fleeing and takes their heads
canary: CANARY — the standing two-clause test. Both halves must still land; nothing about this change should touch it.

description: a brass tyrant whose furnace breath terrifies and whose hammer finds the terrified
canary: CANARY — the payoff sheet. payoffReachable and advantageReachable are siblings now; the payoff must still ship and its save must not be Strength.

description: a bog hound that drags what it bites into the mire
canary: FEATURE — a grappler donor whose grapple row should SURVIVE, so the Advantage clause is legitimate and must be kept.

description: a gullet-worm that swallows what it seizes
canary: FEATURE — grapple into swallow. The clause should stand: the sheet imposes Grappled.

description: a bell-ghost whose toll deafens and whose reach finds the deafened
canary: FEATURE — the GM typed the pairing. Deafened imposed by one row, exploited by another: the engine should let both stand.

description: a lamp-eyed stalker that strikes from the dark
canary: FEATURE — a lurker with no grapple anywhere. If a grappler donor is drawn, the clause must leave.

description: a tide-hag who charms sailors and drowns the charmed
canary: FEATURE — a Charmed pairing rather than Grappled; the rule must read the declared condition, not one word list.

description: a slab-golem that pins a foe underfoot and grinds
canary: FEATURE — pin then grind. Both the Advantage clause and a payoff may be in play on one sheet.

description: a carrion ape that beats the fallen
canary: FEATURE — Prone-keyed pairing. Does anything impose Prone, and does the clause match what does?
